name: Snowy 2.0
summary: A pumped-hydro power station joining two existing dams in the Snowy Mountains scheme. The estimates do not include upgrades to the shared transmission network, which Snowy Hydro does not own. Snowy Hydro says the $22.2bn target cost is not the amount taxpayers will have to fund.
item_keys: snowy hydro limited loan|snowy hydro limited investment
funding_note: The government’s loans and equity to Snowy Hydro also support the Hunter Power Project.

name: Hunter Power Project (Kurri Kurri power station)
summary: A 660 MW gas-fired power station at Kurri Kurri in the Hunter Valley, NSW. The estimates cover the power station only, not the gas pipeline that supplies it. Snowy Hydro said in July 2026 that a final commissioning stage would start testing on or after 10 July 2026.
item_keys: snowy hydro limited loan|snowy hydro limited investment

name: Marinus Link
summary: An undersea electricity link between Tasmania and Victoria, planned as two 750 MW cables. In 2023 the governments that own it agreed to build Stage 1, one cable, first. Supporting transmission in north-west Tasmania is a separate project.

name: Inland Rail
owner: Inland Rail Pty Ltd, formerly part of the Australian Rail Track Corporation (ARTC)
summary: A freight railway from Melbourne to Brisbane. In May 2026 the government decided to finish construction between Beveridge in Victoria and Parkes in New South Wales by the end of 2027, and to preserve the corridor north of Parkes.
funding_note: The 2026-27 Budget counts ARTC’s equity in “Net other” for commercial sensitivity, and returns $4.4bn of equity to the Budget.

name: National Broadband Network
summary: Planned in 2009 as fibre to the premises; changed in 2013 to a mix of technologies. Declared built and fully operational in December 2020. Equity added since then for fibre upgrades is new work and is not included in these estimates.
